speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin, could you describe the nature of your gait and limb ataxia, and when did these symptoms first appear?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any headaches, nausea, or changes in your vision or speech? Also, have you had any recent head injuries or infections?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and current use of natalizumab, I need to rule out Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain_with_contrast

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). Comments: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings confirm Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy, likely caused by the natalizumab therapy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
